facts: Residential facade, no shop. Red-brown brick with broad continuous cream lintel bands and thin sill bands; four bays on four upper rows plus four parlor openings (middle pair close together). Rust-brown open iron escape on four upper levels. Two lower barred openings, right ochre door numbered 339, round caged lamps, low iron well fence and four-lid black refuse enclosure.
Plain raised brick parapet without projecting cornice. 339 touches 341 and 337; no alley. Outer-bay rectangular vents beneath windows.

Right ochre single leaf has square upper glass, 339 below glass and faint 339 at lintel; two round caged lamps above each side, intercom/camera at right. Low barred west/central openings extend into well. Four adjacent sloped lids on black refuse storage enclosure; access lane at right stays clear.

Four upper rows of four sash windows, taupe/brown painted brick and simple cream trapezoid heads; black four-level escape with fine scrolls, dark bracketed cornice with central roof ladder notch. Cornice visibly below 339 and 335. Mapped height 18.93 contradicts this front silhouette; estimated front mass 15.9m against mapped neighbors, not survey measurement. No evidence for assigning 18.93 to a guessed taller rear volume.
